key_facts: On Sept. 22, 2023, Swift driver recruiters Robin Kaufman and Matt Hutto emailed Plaintiff through Tenstreet about completing a driver application. On Sept. 25, Tenstreet posted a DriverIQ employment document and an FMCSA Clearinghouse result; FMCSA emailed that SWIFT TRANSPORTATION CO OF ARIZONA LLC (USDOT 54283) had requested Clearinghouse access. On Sept. 26, Swift Recruiting emailed an encrypted pre-adverse letter (still unread). On Oct. 5, Swift sent a post-adverse letter stating it had decided not to employ Plaintiff based in whole or in part on consumer reports from Asurint, Tenstreet, DriverIQ, FMCSA-DOT, and Equifax Work Number. The uploaded packet is the cover letter and rights summaries, not the underlying reports. No job title or pay is in the file. The load-bearing theory is information-and-belief use of § 290.46 disclosures. Clearinghouse/PSP are drug-alcohol and crash/inspection screens, not Megan's Law. Supporting inference, not proof of Swift's file: written admission of report use, contemporaneous registry listing, and the July 2024 First Advantage/UPS report matching this Plaintiff to SOURCE OF RECORD: CALIFORNIA SEX OFFENDER REGISTRY. That UPS report is not alleged to have been sent to Swift.
procedural_status: Verified complaint review draft generated for proposed September 8, 2026 execution; deliberately unsigned and unfiled. Pre-execution gates: (1) confirm the driver role, terminal, and whether any offer issued; (2) decrypt or obtain the Sept. 26 pre-adverse packet; (3) confirm nonreceipt of the underlying Asurint/Tenstreet/DriverIQ reports; (4) confirm Swift stated no independent lawful ground; (5) verify the current California agent (proposed: National Registered Agents, Inc.); (6) execute on or after September 8 only after those confirmations, and file before September 26, 2026 if the pre-adverse date is treated as accrual. No CRD charge. No demand. Filing court is San Joaquin Superior Court. Companion Judicial Council forms are not yet generated.
damages: No wage rate or hours are in the record. Portfolio valuation is $0 until the role and the reports are documented. Contingent statutory remedies if use is proven: Penal Code § 290.46(j)(4)(A) actual/treble with a $250 floor, fees, exemplary damages, or a civil penalty capped at $25,000; ICRAA § 1786.50 actual damages or $10,000, whichever is greater. Do not import UPS/Pilot numbers.
risk: Better documented than Home Depot on report use (written admission) and worse on the hit (no report). Lerma still kills the count if the reports are ordinary court records. Swift will argue FMCSA/CMV screening is 'authorized by law'; the complaint treats Clearinghouse/PSP as non-290 sources. CCP § 340(a) one-year penalty characterization remains a defense argument on the civil-penalty piece. Diversity removal is likely. Serving a terminal instead of the SOS agent would be a service defect. Naming Knight-Swift merely as parent would be a party defect.
